answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may trade, then weight influence by stake and by fees earned from distinct counterparties over time. A sybil attacker must fund every clone and keep them active; splitting one stake among many identities does not multiply voting weight, while coordinated wash trades can be detected and penalized. A comet-themed bot may join a grove of honest traders, but at the nadir of its activity it gains no reputation for free.
